# Fabric decision record

Use D as a legacy-compatible, time-bounded migration bridge, then cut over to B only after ownership, isolation, rollback, recovery, and workload gates pass. A remains a conditional warm-workload optimization; C is rejected because its pooled warm/cold distribution is invalid. This is a bounded decision, not a universal winner.

| claim_id | disposition | evidence | condition | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A-WARM | supported-bounded | BM-A-WARM,BM-B-WARM,BM-D-WARM,BM-C-POOLED | For the supplied warm workload only, A has a 40 ms median from 3 valid samples versus B at 70 ms and D at 85 ms, each from 3 valid samples; invalid pooled C evidence is excluded. | medium |
| A-COLD | unknown | BM-A-COLD | For the supplied cold workload, A has a 200 ms median from 3 recorded samples with 1 censored run; no acceptable-cold threshold or representative execution window is supplied. | low |
| B-ISOLATION | supported-bounded | SEC-B-ISOLATION,SEC-A-BIND | Within the supplied security findings only, B is supported by workspace-only mounts and scoped credentials while A requires structured bind validation; no claim is made beyond these reviewed controls. | medium |
| B-MIGRATION | unknown | CON-MIGRATION | Immediate B migration under the legacy-compatible 14-day requirement is not demonstrated by the constraint itself. | low |
| C-THROUGHPUT | rejected | BM-C-POOLED | BM-C-POOLED has 4 mixed warm/cold samples, is marked invalid, and is excluded because mixed workloads cannot support one throughput distribution; it cannot establish a universal winner. | high |
| D-MIGRATION | conditional | PROP-D,CON-MIGRATION | D is staged only as a legacy-compatible bridge that must pass a timed rehearsal and become active within 14 calendar days; the proposal and deadline constraint do not independently prove delivery. | low |
| D-RECOVERY | unknown | INC-D-RECOVERY | The supplied D incident reports delayed recovery and that the recovery owner was not assigned; recovery completeness remains unestablished until ownership and a timed drill are evidenced. | unknown |
| CON-MIGRATION | binding | CON-MIGRATION | A legacy-compatible stage must be available within 14 calendar days; phase 1 uses D and cannot proceed unless G-D-MIGRATION passes. | high |
| CON-OWNER | binding | CON-OWNER | Cutover is blocked until specifically named cleanup and recovery owners acknowledge the runbook and escalation path. | high |
| CON-ROLLBACK | binding | CON-ROLLBACK | Every cutover must preserve its prior state and pass an executed rollback rehearsal before traffic expansion. | high |

## Benchmark distributions

| evidence | option | workload | n | censored | valid | median_ms | exclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | --- |
| BM-A-WARM | A | warm | 3 | 0 | true | 40 | - |
| BM-A-COLD | A | cold | 3 | 1 | true | 200 | - |
| BM-B-WARM | B | warm | 3 | 0 | true | 70 | - |
| BM-B-COLD | B | cold | 3 | 0 | true | 95 | - |
| BM-C-POOLED | C | pooled-warm-cold | 4 | 0 | false | - | workload-mixed samples cannot support one throughput distribution |
| BM-D-WARM | D | warm | 3 | 0 | true | 85 | - |
| BM-D-COLD | D | cold | 3 | 0 | true | 125 | - |

Phase 1 is owned by the Execution Fabric Migration Team and may activate D only after the 14-day compatibility rehearsal, named-owner check, and rollback rehearsal pass. Phase 2 is owned by Execution Fabric Operations and may cut over to B only after isolation, separated-workload, and rollback gates pass. The executable rollback triggers restore the preserved legacy state from D or the preserved D bridge from B.

Unresolved boundaries are: D's recovery assignee and recovery-time evidence; A's cold acceptance threshold and censoring bound; B's immediate-migration feasibility; all provider guarantees; and benchmark identity, date, window, representativeness, and uncertainty. Identity changes, a stale or changed workload window, and relevant incidents each force an evidence refresh.
